sections.content: Para que (so that, in order that) always takes the subjunctive when the subject of the purpose clause differs from the subject doing the acting -- perfect for describing deliberate policy, where a government or a landlord acted so that someone else would do something. These sentences are taken directly from the previous reading.

items.spanish: Para que Argentina prosperara, argumentaba Alberdi, era necesario atraer masivamente inmigrantes europeos.
items.english: For Argentina to prosper, Alberdi argued, it was necessary to massively attract European immigrants.

items.spanish: Estas políticas fueron diseñadas precisamente para que millones de europeos cruzaran el Atlántico.
items.english: These policies were designed precisely so that millions of Europeans would cross the Atlantic.

items.spanish: Fundaron, para que sus comunidades pudieran ayudarse mutuamente, cientos de sociedades de socorros mutuos.
items.english: They founded, so that their communities could help each other, hundreds of mutual aid societies.

items.spanish: Los gobiernos promovieron la llegada de colonos europeos para que poblaran territorios que consideraban insuficientemente aprovechados.
items.english: Governments promoted the arrival of European settlers so that they would populate territories they considered insufficiently used.

sections.content: Don't confuse para que + subjunctive (different subjects: A acts so that B happens) with para + infinitive (same subject: A acts in order to do something themselves) -- fundaron sociedades para que sus comunidades pudieran... vs. simply fundaron sociedades para ayudar a sus comunidades.
